title: Spend rank within city
statementMd:
Rank customers within their city by total purchase spending (1 = highest spender) using `RANK()`. Show city, rank, name and spend rounded to 2 decimals. Keep ranks 1 and 2, ordered by city, rank, name.

Expected columns: `city`, `rk`, `name`, `spent`.

Tables: `customers`, `accounts`, `transactions`.

**Row order matters** for this problem.
hints: Totals per customer, then rank by city.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH s AS (SELECT c.city, c.name, -SUM(t.amount) AS spent FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.id = t.account_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = a.customer_id WHERE t.kind = 'purchase' GROUP BY c.id), r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY spent DESC) AS rk FROM s) SELECT city, rk, name, ROUND(spent, 2) AS spent FROM r WHERE rk <= 2 ORDER BY city, rk, name;
```
